observations.detail: Auth middleware now stores the raw Bearer token on req.token (alongside req.user) so downstream handlers like logout can access the original token string without re-parsing the Authorization header. This eliminates fragile '(req as any).headers' casts and prevents silent failures in token blacklisting.

Simplified logout handler to use req.token directly instead of re-parsing the Authorization header. The previous implementation used (req as any).headers?.['authorization'] with nested conditionals that could silently skip blacklisting if any step failed. Now the blacklist is guaranteed to receive the token when auth middleware ran.

Strengthened email validation with RFC 5321 max length check (254 chars) and minimum 2-character TLD requirement. The previous regex '^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$' accepted single-char TLDs like user@example.c and had no length limit, enabling potential abuse via oversized inputs.

All 58 tests pass (5 new). New tests cover: logout blacklists token when req.token is set, logout handles missing req.token gracefully, auth middleware propagates raw token to req.token, email >254 chars rejected, single-char TLD rejected. PR #9 opened against feature/jwt-authentication.

Remaining items for production readiness: (1) Rate limiting on /login, /register, /refresh endpoints — integrate with existing sliding-window rate limiter from feature/rate-limiting-middleware branch, (2) Redis-backed token blacklist for multi-server deployments, (3) JWT ID (jti) claim for individual token tracking/revocation, (4) Key ID (kid) header for key rotation support.

The AuthRequest interface in middleware/auth.ts and AuthRouteRequest in routes/auth.ts both gained a 'token?: string' field. These two interfaces are separate but parallel — a future refactor could unify them or have AuthRouteRequest extend AuthRequest to avoid drift.
